In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

protein p270/T pr is a general and constitutive component of the intracellular filaments attached to nucleoplasmic NPC surfaces, but not of the cytoplasmically exposed annulus of NPCs, in diverse vertebrate cells.
p270/Tpr is a general and essential component of the intrapores of the NPC, and that it is not present on the cytoplasm-facing side of the NPC.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
p270/Tpr is not located on the cytoplasm-facing side of the NPC, but is a component of intranuclear NPC-associated filaments.
protein p270/T pr is a constitutive component of the NPC-attached filaments and is located exclusively on the intranuclear face of NPC.
protein p270/TPr is a component of the nuclear envelope that resides exclusively at the nucleoplasm side of NPCs and is thus a bona fide nucleoporin.
The main takeaway from our work is that
protein p270/Trp is a general component of the NPC-attached filaments in all vertebrate cells.

protein p270/Trp, which has been shown by others to be a constituent of the cytoplasmically facing annulus of NPCs (Byr et al., 1994; Sweet et al., 2001), is in fact a component of the intrinsically nuclear NPC-attached filaments.

protein p270/Trp, previously thought to be located at the outer surface of the NPC, is actually a general component of the intracellular filaments that emanate from the NPC and extend into the nucleus.
